title: The Gang of Four and the Design Patterns Book (1994)
explainer: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, and John Vlissides catalogued 23 recurring object-oriented design solutions in their 1994 book Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software, instantly nicknamed 'the Gang of Four' book. It reframed framework and library design as a search for reusable, named structural vocabulary rather than one-off cleverness, a mindset directly relevant to anyone designing a novel system or framework today.

title: Roy Fielding's Dissertation and the Invention of REST (2000)
explainer: REST was not an existing standard someone wrote down - it was coined and formalized in Roy Fielding's 2000 UC Irvine PhD dissertation, which built a general framework of architectural styles and then used it to justify the design choices already implicit in the web's HTTP protocol. It is a striking example of novel system/framework design: an entirely new architectural style, invented and argued for from first principles, that went on to shape how most web APIs are built.
